claim_boundary: Local single-node failure evidence only; no production SLA, HA, multi-GPU, or customer-traffic claim.
corrective_action: Keep the 60-second recovery window and require the experiment API container to be absent before selected-point replay.
Gate terminal GPU utilization by a five-sample median relative to the measured pre-run baseline while retaining every instantaneous sample and maximum in private evidence.
Continue to fail closed on lease mismatch, elevated VRAM, thermal risk, or cleanup failure without weakening the fixed operating latency SLO.
next_action: Validate the baseline-relative quiet gate in a clean external 60 RPS pilot, then restart all 66 acceptance repetitions from one clean revision.
root_cause: The first quiet-gate implementation treated the maximum whole-device utilization sample as experiment-owned activity and required it to be at most 15 percent. The desktop-attached Windows GPU baseline was already 22 percent and the 60-second samples alternated between display-related spikes and low values even though the S4 container was absent after cleanup, memory remained below baseline, and the exact lease matched. The absolute-maximum rule therefore produced a false blocker.
